_doc: M7-05 — the strings the Board screen (S05) shows, and nothing else. It exists because X-04 requires every user-facing string to be a loc key in EN and DE from day one, and because ContentInvariants.CheckLocaleKeyReferences fails a loc key that nothing in the content set names — a key referenced only from C# is an orphan, and an orphan is fatal. This document is that naming. The `block` group is the load-bearing one: a roll can be refused for four different reasons that all arrive on the wire as the single value ILLEGAL_STATE, so the screen names the cause from the run's own state and needs one sentence per cause. The `tile` group carries all fifteen tile names because the run's pending tile arrives as a bare integer and the screen has to say what the player is standing on. The `forkLabel` group is new with the real board: BoardView.Project hands the client the bias label each branch's tiles were actually drawn under, so the two branch buttons name where they go instead of naming their structural position. The `dice` group is the fixed dice (`04` §6): a tray heading over the numbers the run holds, and the prompt that asks the player to name a number for one it has been granted. Neither carries a numeral — a die's number is drawn as a numeral on its own control, which needs no translation. Deliberately absent, each because a later milestone owns it: the perks list, the consumable pouch, and every battle, draft, shop, event and campfire caption. The `action.skipUnbuilt` and `block.unbuiltScreen` pair is the one thing here that is not a finished screen's string: an Event tile and a Minigame tile are each left by a command only their own screen submits, neither screen is built, and RESOLVE_TILE clears neither — so a run that landed on one was parked with the roll refused and ABANDON_RUN as its only exit. The board resolves them through their own commands instead, and these two strings are what it says while doing so: the control admits it is skipping rather than continuing, and the sentence names the missing screen. Both go when the screens land. Gone rather than absent: the reroll's caption, its 'changes the next roll' sentence, its exhausted-refusal line and the die panel's control, all removed with the reroll and the die's special faces.
